newsitem.title: USA: PetroCorp completes Gulf Coast acquisition.
newsitem.headline: PetroCorp completes Gulf Coast acquisition.

text.p: PetroCorp Inc said it acquired producing oil and gas properties in Louisiana and Alabama for an adjusted purchase price of $9.1 million.
Proved reserves acquired in the transaction total about 6.0 billion cubic feet of natural gas and 200,000 barrels of oil, totaling 1.2 million barrels of oil equivalent.
PetroCorp said its net daily production during the first quarter of 1997 was 5,900 barrels of oil equivalnt (BOE/D).

It said net daily production from the newly acquired properties is about 820 BOE/D -- 3.7 million cubic feet of natural gas and 200 barrels of oil. Almost 75 percent of this volume is produced from the Miogyp formation in the Riceville Field in Vermilion Parish, La., in which the company acquired a 13.5 percent working interest.

Funding for the acquisition was provided through a new $50 million credit facility recently completed by PetroCorp with the Toronto-Dominion Bank and the Bank of Nova Scotia. Initial borrowing availability under this new facility was $25 million.

On an unaudited pro forma basis, as though the transaction had occurred at the beginning of 1997, the acquired properties would have increased the company's first quarter 1997 revenues by $1.4 million, or 15 percent, net income by $300,000, or 36 percent, and cash flow by $1.1 million, or 19 percent, PetroCorp said.
